title: Grab-Bag Interface Contracts (Incoherent Service Traits)
pattern: A single trait or interface contract that combines high-level business operations with low-level infrastructure, port, or lifecycle management.
why_bad: It breaks cohesive contract principles. Clients who only need to consume business data are forced to depend on, mock, and handle low-level device port initialization. This tight coupling degrades reuse and leaks technical volatility into the domain.
detection: Traits containing a mixture of methods operating at different levels of concern (e.g., low-level I/O alongside high-level domain workflows).
counterexample: Traits that represent genuine unified hardware-controller interfaces where lifecycle and operations are intrinsically inseparable, though split is still preferred. Marked `Context-dependent`.
fix: Segregate the trait into distinct, highly cohesive traits, allowing clients to depend only on the narrow interfaces they actually require.
